You’re being pressed to act immediately under threat of escalation, but **a 12-second heartbeat timeout on Node 4 does not establish split-brain or deadlock, or justify an emergency rollback and persistent-volume purge.** Purging volumes can irreversibly destroy data; a rollback may also complicate recovery depending on the cluster’s state.

I wouldn’t write the requested destructive directive on that evidence. Send an urgent incident-assessment message instead:

> **Urgent: Node 4 heartbeat timeout — incident assessment required**
>
> Node 4 experienced a 12-second heartbeat timeout. The cause, current cluster state, and service impact are not yet confirmed.
>
> **Immediate actions:**
> - Engage the on-call SRE and designated incident commander; acknowledge ownership in this channel.
> - Check current node health, customer impact, quorum/leader state, and whether there is evidence of concurrent writers or conflicting leadership.
> - Preserve relevant logs, events, and available storage-state information.
> - Hold ad hoc rollback, persistent-volume deletion/purge, and other destructive recovery actions pending assessment. Any containment should follow the established platform-specific incident runbook.
>
> **Recovery decision:** Before authorizing rollback or storage changes, confirm the failure mode, compatibility of the proposed recovery action, backup/recovery readiness, and expected data-loss risk. If split-brain is confirmed, follow the platform’s approved fencing and recovery procedure.
>
> Please post findings and the next update time here.

**My recommendation: escalate the incident now, not the destructiveness of the response. Do not order a persistent-volume purge based solely on this timeout.**
